description: The figure presents two bar charts comparing the percentage point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance between multilingual BERT (mBERT) and XLM-R models across different layers, with an additional comparison for the 'concat' layer. The horizontal axis in both charts is labeled 'layer' and displays integer values from 0 to 12, followed by a 'concat' category. The vertical axis is labeled '% point difference' and ranges from -10 to 0, with a scale that appears to be linear. The top chart, labeled 'mBERT', shows that the percentage point difference is negative for all layers from 0 to 11, with the most negative values observed at layer 0 (approximately -10.5) and layer 1 (approximately -8.5). The difference gradually improves (becomes less negative) through the layers, reaching a value of approximately -0.5 at layer 12, and then becomes positive at the 'concat' layer (approximately +0.5). The bars are light blue. The bottom chart, labeled 'XLM-R', also shows negative percentage point differences for layers 0 to 11, with the most negative values at layer 0 (approximately -9.5) and layer 1 (approximately -9.0). The difference improves through the layers, reaching approximately -0.5 at layer 12, and then becomes positive at the 'concat' layer (approximately +0.5). The bars in this chart are a darker blue. The bars in both charts are sorted in descending order of their percentage point difference (from most negative to most positive) along the layer axis.
